chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the man whose matter has grieved him or who desires a need, he said: 'He should pray two Rak'at, reciting in one of them "Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad" a thousand times, and in the other once. Then he should ask for his need.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed method for praying to fulfill a specific need or remove grief according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi prescribes a specific two-rak'ah prayer for fulfilling needs, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas one thousand times in the first rak'ah and once in the second, a practice rooted in the concept of divine unity as a means of spiritual focus. Scholarly tradition highlights this as a method of concentrating the heart on Allah's essence to facilitate the granting of requests, reflecting the Shia emphasis on specific devotional acts (Mu'ajjalat) for spiritual and worldly benefits. The disparity in recitation counts underscores the importance of repetition (Tawarrud) in intensifying supplication.
